---
title: "attr() completes attribute names, until a second one starts the same way"
ref: IDX-07
categories: [Indexing]
impact: silencieux
extrait: 'attr(structure(1:3, unit = "cm"), "u")'
reponse: '"cm"'
attendu: "`NULL`, there is no attribute named u"
versions: "All"
source: "hadley/strict"
---

::: {.piege}
```{r}
measure <- structure(1:3, unit = "cm")
attr(measure, "u")
measure <- structure(1:3, unit = "cm", uncertainty = 0.1)
attr(measure, "u")
```
:::

## Why

The `exact` argument of `attr()` is `FALSE` by default: a prefix is enough, as long as only one attribute starts with it. R returns that attribute without a warning.

The day another attribute starts with the same letters, here `uncertainty` next to `unit`, the prefix becomes ambiguous and `attr()` returns `NULL`. The code that reads the attribute has not changed.

## The remedy

Write the full name with `exact = TRUE`, or ask R to flag every partial match.

::: {.piege}
```{r}
attr(measure, "unit", exact = TRUE)
options(warnPartialMatchAttr = TRUE)
attr(structure(1:3, unit = "cm"), "u")
```
:::
